title: Beyond Just Color
context: Color vision differences and conveying meaning
whyItMatters: Color is a useful design signal, but relying on one hue alone can leave some people without the information it carries.
learningObjectives: Understand why color alone is not enough to convey information.
Identify lightness contrast as a secondary visual cue.
Pair color changes with other indicators.
lessonParagraphs: Color often acts as shorthand in an interface. A red outline can imply an error, and a green button can suggest success. If color is the only signal, people who perceive those hues differently may miss the meaning.
Lightness contrast provides another cue that does not depend on hue. Even when two colors appear similar, a difference between light and dark can help keep elements distinct.
Pair a color change with a shape or text cue. An error field can use an icon or a strong underline, and a text link can use an underline or heavier weight as well as color.
Treating color as a supporting signal helps an interface remain understandable across different ways of seeing.
